facts.fact_text: On 14 March 2017, in response to the call by Mr Navalnyy to protest against corruption, the applicant notified the Kazan Town Administration of her intention to hold a meeting from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. on 26 March 2017.
The aim of the meeting notified by the applicant on 14 March 2017 was to protest against corruption and to demand Mr Medvedev's resignation.
On 17 March 2017, the applicant and Mr B. notified the Kazan Town Administration of their intention to hold a "picket" (пикетирование) against corruption from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. on 26 March 2017.

In the VKontakte message of 23 March 2017, the applicant stated that people were entitled to assemble peacefully and that it had therefore been decided to hold a meeting in Krylya Sovetov Park at 2 p.m. on 26 March 2017 to protest against corruption.

The VKontakte message of 23 March 2017 ended with the following call: "Invite your friends to join the group. We demand answers in the streets of Kazan! The meeting point is near the main entrance to Krylya Sovetov Park in Kopylova street, underground station Aviastroitelnaya."
On 26 March 2017, the applicant held a meeting at the specially designated location for public events in Krylya Sovetov Park.
According to the applicant, about 1,500 people attended the meeting held in Krylya Sovetov Park on 26 March 2017.
According to the applicant, the meeting held in Krylya Sovetov Park on 26 March 2017 lasted for about one hour and twenty minutes.
On 16 March 2017, the Kazan Town Administration refused to approve the meeting notified by the applicant on 14 March 2017.

On 21 March 2017, the Kazan Town Administration refused to approve the "picket" notified on 17 March 2017, claiming that other (unspecified) public events were scheduled at the locations chosen by the applicant at the same time.

On 24 March 2017, the Kazan department of internal affairs warned the applicant that if she held a public event at one of the locations indicated in her notifications of 14 and 17 March 2017, she would be held liable.
According to the Government, during the meeting in Krylya Sovetov Park on 26 March 2017, the police used loudspeakers to order the participants to disperse.
According to the applicant, a police officer approached her during the meeting in Krylya Sovetov Park on 26 March 2017 and demanded that she stop the unlawful public event.
The applicant was arrested on her way home after the meeting in Krylya Sovetov Park at about 4.20 p.m. on 26 March 2017.
At 6 p.m. on 26 March 2017, the police drew up a report on an administrative offence under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences against the applicant.
At 6 p.m. on 26 March 2017, the police also drew up a report on an administrative offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences against the applicant.

On 27 March 2017, the Aviastroitelnyy District Court of Kazan, in two separate judgments, found the applicant guilty of offences under Articles 19.3 and 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Aviastroitelnyy District Court of Kazan sentenced the applicant to a fine of 1,000 Russian roubles under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Aviastroitelnyy District Court of Kazan sentenced the applicant to twenty hours of community work under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
On 12 July 2017, the Vakhitovskiy District Court of Kazan found the applicant guilty of an offence under Article 20.2 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Vakhitovskiy District Court of Kazan ordered the applicant to pay a fine of 10,000 Russian roubles for the offence under Article 20.2 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Kazan Town Administration's refusal of 16 March 2017 was based on the claim that other (unspecified) public events were scheduled at the locations chosen by the applicant at the same time.

On 21 March 2017, the Kazan Town Administration refused to approve the "picket" notified on 17 March 2017, claiming that other (unspecified) public events were scheduled at the locations chosen by the applicant at the same time.

The Vakhitovskiy District Court of Kazan found that the regional branch of the "United Russia" party had earlier notified the Kazan Town Administration of its intention to hold public events from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. on 26 March 2017 at all three locations chosen by the applicant and at two other sites.

The Vakhitovskiy District Court of Kazan found that in the circumstances where the regional branch of the "United Russia" party had notified the Kazan Town Administration of events at the same locations, the town administration was required to provide the applicant with well-reasoned proposals for changing the location or time of her intended meeting.
The Vakhitovskiy District Court of Kazan found that the Kazan Town Administration had not made any well-reasoned proposals for changing the location or time of the applicant's intended meeting.
The Vakhitovskiy District Court of Kazan found that the Kazan Town Administration's failure to propose an alternative location or time for the applicant's event had been unlawful.

The Aviastroitelnyy District Court of Kazan did not reply to the applicant's argument that the Kazan Town Administration's decision of 16 March 2017 refusing to approve the meeting had been annulled on judicial review and that the meeting had therefore to be considered as authorised and lawful, and the police's order to stop it unlawful.

In her appeal, the applicant referred to the decision of 24 March 2017 by the Vakhitovskiy District Court of Kazan declaring unlawful the Kazan Town Administration's decision of 16 March 2017 refusing to approve the meeting.

In her appeal, the applicant submitted that under Article 227 § 8 of the Code of Administrative Procedure, the Vakhitovskiy District Court's decision of 24 March 2017 was subject to immediate enforcement.

In her appeal, the applicant referred to a Constitutional Court ruling of 14 February 2013 that a public event was considered to be approved not only after receipt by the organiser of the local authorities' express approval, but also if the local authorities had not provided the organiser with a well-reasoned proposal for a change of location or time of the event within the statutory time-limit.

The Supreme Court of the Tatarstan Republic held that the judicial decision finding the Kazan Town Administration's failure to act unlawful did not amount to an unconditional approval of the location and time of the public event and did not exempt the organiser from fulfilling the obligations imposed by the Public Events Act.

The Supreme Court of the Tatarstan Republic held that the judicial decision finding the Kazan Town Administration's failure to act unlawful did not transform an unauthorised public event into an authorised one.

The Supreme Court of the Tatarstan Republic held that the argument that the public event was to be considered as approved if the local authorities had not provided the organiser with a well-reasoned proposal for a change of location or time within the statutory time-limit was invalid in the present case.

For a summary of the domestic provisions on the procedure for the notification and conduct of public events, on relevant judicial review procedures and on the liability for breaches committed in the course of public events, see Lashmankin and Others v. Russia, nos. 57818/09 and 14 others, § 216-312, 7 February 2017.

Plenary Supreme Court Ruling no. 28 of 26 June 2018 provides that failure to comply with the three-day statutory time-limit for proposing a change of location or time means that the public event must be considered to be approved by default (point 10).

Plenary Supreme Court Ruling no. 28 of 26 June 2018 provides that it is not necessary to notify a public event planned at a specially designated location for public events, provided that the number of participants does not exceed the number permitted for each such location by regional law (point 15).

Plenary Supreme Court Ruling no. 28 of 26 June 2018 provides that the public authority may propose a change of location or time of a public event to be held at a specially designated location and not requiring notification only if another public event has been scheduled to take place at the same location and time and either (i) the number of participants of the two simultaneous events will exceed the maximum capacity of the location, or (ii) it will not be possible to ensure the peaceful character of the simultaneous events by applying security arrangements habitually used at public events with a comparable number of participants (point 15).

The report on the administrative offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences stated that the applicant had disobeyed a lawful order of the police and had thereby committed an offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

The Supreme Court of the Tatarstan Republic held that the evidence cumulatively showed that the applicant had disobeyed a lawful order by a police officer who was fulfilling his duty to safeguard public order and ensure public safety.

The Supreme Court of the Tatarstan Republic held that the police officer acted within the powers provided by law with the aim of fulfilling his duty to ensure public safety and order, and that his order to stop the public event addressed to its organiser could be considered lawful in accordance with the Police Act.

The applicant proposed three alternative sites for the Kazan Town Administration to choose from for the meeting planned for 26 March 2017, including a specially designated location for holding public events in Krylya Sovetov Park.
On 21 March 2017, the Kazan Town Administration proposed another venue for the "picket" notified on 17 March 2017.
On 22 March 2017, the applicant accepted the venue proposed by the Kazan Town Administration for the "picket".

In the VKontakte message of 23 March 2017, the applicant claimed that the Kazan Town Administration could not refuse to allow the meeting in Krylya Sovetov Park because it was a specially designated location for public events.
In the VKontakte message of 23 March 2017, the applicant stated that if another event was scheduled at Krylya Sovetov Park, the Kazan Town Administration had to propose another time for the meeting.
In the VKontakte message of 23 March 2017, the applicant stated that Krylya Sovetov Park was very large and there was enough space for several simultaneous events.
On 24 March 2017, the Vakhitovskiy District Court of Kazan allowed the applicant's claim against the Kazan Town Administration's decision of 16 March 2017 in part.

The Vakhitovskiy District Court of Kazan found that in the circumstances where the regional branch of the "United Russia" party had notified the Kazan Town Administration of events at the same locations, the town administration was required to provide the applicant with well-reasoned proposals for changing the location or time of her intended meeting.
The Vakhitovskiy District Court of Kazan found that the Kazan Town Administration had not made any well-reasoned proposals for changing the location or time of the applicant's intended meeting.
The Vakhitovskiy District Court of Kazan found that the Kazan Town Administration's failure to propose an alternative location or time for the applicant's event had been unlawful.
On 26 March 2017, the applicant held a meeting at the specially designated location for public events in Krylya Sovetov Park.
According to the applicant, she replied to the police officer's demand by referring to the Vakhitovskiy District Court's decision of 24 March 2017 and stating that the meeting was lawful.
According to the applicant, no further action was taken by the police until the end of the meeting in Krylya Sovetov Park on 26 March 2017.

The Aviastroitelnyy District Court of Kazan did not reply to the applicant's argument that the Kazan Town Administration's decision of 16 March 2017 refusing to approve the meeting had been annulled on judicial review and that the meeting had therefore to be considered as authorised and lawful, and the police's order to stop it unlawful.

In her appeal, the applicant submitted that under Article 227 § 8 of the Code of Administrative Procedure, the Vakhitovskiy District Court's decision of 24 March 2017 was subject to immediate enforcement.

In her appeal, the applicant argued that the public event had not created any risk to people's lives or health or to the property of persons or legal entities.
In her appeal, the applicant argued that the participants had not committed any unlawful acts or breached the procedure for the conduct of public events established by the Public Events Act.
In her appeal, the applicant argued that there had been no lawful grounds to stop the public event.

The Supreme Court of the Tatarstan Republic held that the judicial decision finding the Kazan Town Administration's failure to act unlawful did not amount to an unconditional approval of the location and time of the public event and did not exempt the organiser from fulfilling the obligations imposed by the Public Events Act.

The Supreme Court of the Tatarstan Republic held that the judicial decision finding the Kazan Town Administration's failure to act unlawful did not transform an unauthorised public event into an authorised one.

The Supreme Court of the Tatarstan Republic found that the aim of the public event indicated in the notification (against corruption and for Prime Minister Medvedev's resignation) differed from the real aim of the public event and the aim declared during preliminary campaigning for that event.

The Supreme Court of the Tatarstan Republic noted that on 23 March 2017 the applicant had published on her VKontakte personal page campaigning material about the forthcoming public event at 2 p.m. on 26 March 2017 in Krylya Sovetov Park, which stated: "26 March is a nationwide protest day against corruption by Russian high-ranking officials. #whereisDimon#lookforDimon. Friends, we have the right to assemble peacefully, to discuss. It has therefore been decided to hold the meeting in Krylya Sovetov Park ...".

The Vakhitovskiy District Court of Kazan found that on 23 March 2017 the applicant had published a message on VKontakte calling for participation in a meeting to be held on 26 March 2017 in Krylya Sovetov Park, despite the fact that the Kazan Town Administration had refused to approve that meeting and had suggested that the applicant should hold a "picket" at another location.

The Vakhitovskiy District Court of Kazan found that the applicant had campaigned for participation in the public event before it had been approved by the competent regional or municipal authorities, contrary to the applicable law.

The Supreme Court of the Tatarstan Republic held that section 10 § 1 of the Public Events Act expressly prohibited organisers from campaigning for participation in a public event before it had been approved by the competent local authorities.

The Supreme Court of the Tatarstan Republic held that the applicant had breached the prohibition in section 10 § 1 of the Public Events Act against campaigning for participation in a public event before it had been approved by the competent local authorities.

Plenary Supreme Court Ruling no. 28 of 26 June 2018 provides that courts must take into account that a proposal to change the location or time of a public event or the manner of conducting it must not be arbitrary or unreasoned, and must mention specific facts showing that public interest considerations make it manifestly impossible to hold the public event at the chosen location or time (point 12).

Plenary Supreme Court Ruling no. 28 of 26 June 2018 provides that inconvenience caused to citizens by a public event or an assumption by the authorities that there might be a risk of such inconvenience may not in themselves be considered valid reasons for changing the location or time of a public event (point 12).

Plenary Supreme Court Ruling no. 28 of 26 June 2018 provides that it is not necessary to notify a public event planned at a specially designated location for public events, provided that the number of participants does not exceed the number permitted for each such location by regional law (point 15).

Plenary Supreme Court Ruling no. 28 of 26 June 2018 provides that if a court allowed the administrative complaint before the planned date of the public event, it may require the public authority not to impede the public event at the location and time chosen by the organisers (point 20).
